PUBLIC RESPONSE: Agency Law

The mid-1960s codification sequence supplies the clearest chronological anchor. Enacted in 1965, the Agency Law placed the explicit “tom lev” duty in operative provisions (§§6 and 8) governing the agent’s conduct toward the principal, at a time when no post-1948 Israeli statute had yet done so. Later instruments—the Pledges Law 1967, Sale Law 1968 §6, and Contracts (General Part) Law 1973—simply extended or generalized language already present in the 1965 text. Assertions that the Agency Law omits the phrase rest on secondary recollection rather than the enacted wording itself; once the statutory language is consulted directly, the 1965 enactment is shown to be the earliest explicit introduction.
